OMEGA-ISOP — TARGETED CATEGORY AUDIT: AMALGAMATION DOES NOT IMPLY COLIMIT
DOCUMENT_ID: OI-STAGE-02-AMALGAMATION-COLIMIT-AUDIT-2026-10-28
VERSION: 0.2
DATE: 2026-10-29
STATUS: FINITE CONDITIONAL OBSTRUCTION PROVED; CORE-LEVEL COLIMIT STATUS OPEN
SCOPE: Test whether the Volume II compatibility condition CC(C1,C2)=1, defined by existence of an admissible amalgamation, is by itself enough to establish a categorical colimit.

SOURCE ALIGNMENT
The protected Library source Volume II specifies:
- configurations C=(S_C,#_C), with #_C the selected apartness structure;
- embeddings that are injective and preserve and reflect apartness;
- CC(C1,C2)=1 iff an admissible amalgamation exists;
- R := colim(D_CC) only where the required categorical construction exists;
- a valid indexing category, functor/diagram, relevant morphisms, and colimit existence/universal property are required.
This audit tests one explicit category-level realization of those definitions. It does not assert that this realization is the unique or intended project realization.

1. TEST CATEGORY
Let C be the category whose objects are finite sets X equipped with the discrete apartness relation
x # y iff x != y,
and whose morphisms are embeddings: injective functions preserving and reflecting #.
In this category, every injective function between objects is an embedding, and every morphism is injective.

2. NONTRIVIAL SPAN OF CONFIGURATIONS
Let S={s1,s2}, A=S∪{a}, and B=S∪{b}, where s1,s2,a,b are pairwise distinct and every pair of distinct elements is apart. Consider the span
A <- S -> B,
where both arrows are inclusions. Each of S, A, and B has at least two elements, so the example does not rely on a singleton configuration.

An admissible amalgam exists: take C0=S∪{a,b}, with discrete apartness, and the evident embeddings A -> C0 and B -> C0 that agree on S. Thus, under the existence-of-amalgam criterion, CC(A,B)=1 for this span.

3. CLAIM
The span A <- S -> B has no pushout in the stated category of finite discrete-apartness structures and embeddings.

4. PROOF BY CONTRADICTION
Assume a pushout P exists, with embeddings j_A:A -> P and j_B:B -> P agreeing on S.

First use the cocone into C0=S∪{a,b}, where the images of a and b remain distinct. The pushout universal property supplies a morphism h0:P -> C0 factoring the two embeddings. Since every morphism in this category is injective, the images j_A(a) and j_B(b) must be distinct in P.

Now let Z=S∪{z}, where z is distinct from s1 and s2, again with discrete apartness. Define embeddings f:A -> Z and g:B -> Z by fixing both elements of S and mapping both a and b to z. Each map is individually injective, and they agree on S, so they form a valid cocone over the span. The pushout universal property would give a morphism hZ:P -> Z satisfying hZ∘j_A=f and hZ∘j_B=g. But j_A(a) and j_B(b) are distinct in P while both must map to z. Therefore hZ is not injective, contradicting the requirement that every morphism in the category be an embedding. Hence no pushout exists. QED.

5. INTERPRETATION
The example uses only configurations of size at least two and establishes a strict distinction:
- WEAK AMALGAMATION: some object C receives embeddings of A and B that agree on the shared base.
- CATEGORICAL PUSHOUT: an amalgam satisfies the universal property for every compatible cocone in the specified category.

The first does not imply the second in the tested category. Therefore CC(C1,C2)=1, when defined only by existence of an admissible amalgamation, does not by itself prove that the corresponding span has a colimit. The existence of an amalgam and the existence of a colimit are logically different claims.

6. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH
PROVED: In the explicit category defined in Section 1, the displayed span has an admissible amalgam but no pushout.
PROVED: The stated CC criterion alone cannot be used as a general proof of colimit existence across all categories of configurations and embeddings.
NOT PROVED: That the Frozen Core's particular R=colim(D_CC) fails to exist.
NOT PROVED: That every possible configuration category or every alternative morphism class lacks the required colimits.
NOT DERIVED: A project-level obstruction to R without the actual selected indexing category, diagram, morphisms, and target category.

7. REQUIRED NEXT FORMALIZATION
To instantiate the Core's conditional construction, specify:
(a) the object class of admissible configurations;
(b) the exact morphisms and their composition;
(c) the indexing category J, including arrows encoding compatibility;
(d) the target category C_METACORE and a functor D:J -> C_METACORE;
(e) the cocone candidate for R;
(f) the universal property to be proved, or an explicitly equivalent constraint-preserving construction.
Then test whether the chosen category admits the relevant colimit. If embeddings are retained as morphisms, the example above warns that ordinary weak amalgamation is insufficient. A different morphism class, a restricted cocone class, or a stronger amalgamation condition may alter the result, but any such choice must be explicit and justified.

8. DECISION
Record this as a finite conditional obstruction against the inference “admissible amalgam exists, therefore categorical colimit exists.” Preserve the Core's conditional R construction. Do not declare the Core inconsistent or R impossible. Do not advance to Constraint or dynamic realization on this result alone.

CHANGE CONTROL
Candidate audit only. Frozen Core unchanged. No RL registration performed or verified. No CE-V promotion or canonical acceptance claimed.

END OF DOCUMENT
